title: Smallpox inoculation spreads West
place: London, England and Boston, United States
summary: Inoculation against smallpox, long practised in Asia and Africa, was promoted in Britain by Lady Mary Wortley Montagu and in Boston via the enslaved African Onesimus.

unsung.contribution: Taught Cotton Mather the African practice of variolation, which Mather promoted in Boston's 1721 smallpox outbreak.
unsung.recognition: Recognition came largely in modern times, such as Boston magazine naming him among the best Bostonians in 2016.
